title: quimby territory transition operating plan
instruction:
You are Ivy Marchbanks, sales director at Quimby Irrigation Supply, and I need you to prepare the territory transition operating plan that Dale Prendergast will read on Monday morning before we meet with him. Quimby is standing up an inside-sales desk for the commercial-landscape segment. In P11, 31 of Dale’s accounts move to that desk, cutting a 28-year field representative’s book by about a fifth. The plan has to tell him plainly which accounts move, when the change takes effect, and what the change does to his commission; it also needs to make a credible case for why this is the right operating decision without treating the person who built the book as an afterthought. Use the attached `quimby_transition_review_packet.xlsx`, which contains the current account information, commission materials, the working draft, and comments from Gerhard Moravec, Astrid Rivenburgh, Sofia Skarsgard, Tamsin Elbaz, and Naledi Kavanagh. Treat the packet as the source of truth for account names, segment status, timing, sales figures, and commission terms, and revise the draft rather than creating a generic change-management note. Put the finished file in the top level of the working directory using exactly the filename `quimby_territory_transition_operating_plan.docx`. Keep it to no more than three pages, because Dale needs to read it before the Monday conversation and senior leadership needs to reuse it as the meeting brief. Make the document an operating plan rather than a speech: 1) give Dale a concise statement of the decision and the business reason; 2) provide a complete, auditable account-level view of all 31 transfers, including the effective timing and any accounts that remain with him where that distinction matters; 3) show the commission effect using the packet’s figures, with the same baseline, transferred-book amount, and resulting impact wherever those figures appear; 4) set out the transition ownership, customer handoff expectations, and protections against service disruption; 5) address the review comments and any changed facts in the packet, making clear what was changed from the working draft; and 6) end with one recommendation and a clear decision statement, not a menu of options or a list of future work. We cannot spend a month shadowing every account before Monday, and the inside-sales desk has limited onboarding capacity, so make a defensible choice about what must happen before the effective date and what can be handled during the transition; do not hide that tradeoff. Also draw a clear boundary between commitments Quimby must make to customers and Dale and improvements that would merely be desirable, since the packet does not make every good idea feasible immediately. Put the gains from the new segment and the losses to Dale close enough together that the reader can assess the tradeoff honestly. Do not invent commission rates, account facts, customer promises, legal conclusions, or performance guarantees that are not supported by the packet, and do not include system click-by-click instructions or a separate compensation-policy rewrite. The result should be usable by Dale, Ivy, and a senior decision maker without asking you what the account list, timing, financial effect, owners, or decision actually are.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/quimby_transition_review_packet.xlsx` — Source packet containing the current account roster and segment classifications, commission terms and figures, the working transition draft, explicit review comments, and changed operational facts needed to revise the plan.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `quimby_territory_transition_operating_plan.docx` — A decision-ready territory transition operating plan for Dale Prendergast and senior leadership. (Top level of the starting working directory; exactly three pages or fewer; must include the complete transfer view, commission effect, transition ownership and customer handoff expectations, response to review comments and changed facts, and one final recommendation/decision statement. No system click-through instructions or compensation-policy rewrite.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

Territory Transition Operating Plan
For Dale Prendergast and senior leadership | Decision owner: Ivy Marchbanks | Effective in P11
Decision and candid impact
Quimby Irrigation Supply will move exactly 31 distinct commercial-landscape accounts from Dale Prendergast’s field book to the inside-sales desk in the roster-assigned P11 waves: 04, 11, and 18 Nov 2026. This concentrates the commercial-landscape segment in the desk’s new scope; Dale retains the non-commercial-landscape field book (24 distinct retained accounts shown in the source roster). The operating gain and the loss are inseparable: the desk gains a focused commercial-landscape book, while Dale’s FY26-through-P10 commission baseline loses the transferred-book credit under the current terms.
FY26 through P10 commission view

These are source-supported FY26-through-P10 figures, not a forecast of Dale’s future income or a change to compensation terms. Payroll / Commissions Lead will walk Dale through the account-level calculation and current terms; this plan does not promise retained credit, income, or account ownership.
Operating controls: what must happen vs. what should follow
Boundary
Control
MUST — before each assigned wave
Sales Operations Manager confirms the roster; Inside-Sales Desk Manager accepts each account; handoff record carries open work and customer context; customer receives the named desk contact at or before that wave.
MUST — continuity-sensitive accounts
For any active opportunity, open commitment, open order, or open renewal, Dale and the receiving desk complete a joint review of the flagged item before that account’s wave.
MUST — capacity fallback
Only 12 pre-effective readiness sessions are available; assign them first to the flagged accounts. For other accounts, the accepted handoff record is the minimum and Dale remains available during transition for context—not full pre-transfer shadowing.
SHOULD — after transfer
The desk may deepen relationship history and pursue additional joint introductions during transition. These are improvements, not conditions that delay the P11 move.
Ownership, escalation, and monitoring
Accountability
Owner
Control
Transfer decision and exceptions
Ivy Marchbanks, Sales Director
Confirms decision; receives same-business-day escalation.

Named contact at/before wave; joint review where flagged.

Sales Operations Manager / Payroll & Commissions Lead
At each wave close, reconcile all roster accounts, acceptance, and customer-contact status; explain current-term calculation.
Trigger: a disputed handoff or any condition that could interrupt service, an open commitment, or an active opportunity is escalated by the Inside-Sales Desk Manager to Ivy the same business day. The wave-close reconciliation is complete only when each moved account is accepted and its customer-contact and handoff record are recorded.

Revision record and decision
This plan replaces the 10 Oct working draft using the review packet’s current facts. The changes are material, not editorial:
What changed
Source
Plan treatment
Timing and scope
Gerhard Moravec / current facts
Replaced P10 and “approximately 30” with the complete 31-account roster and P11 waves: 04, 11, and 18 Nov 2026.
Comparison and rationale
Astrid Rivenburgh / current facts
Made commercial-landscape scope explicit and identified the 24 retained non-commercial-landscape field accounts.
Commission clarity
Sofia Skarsgard / Commission terms

Feasible preparation
Tamsin Elbaz / current facts
Removed all-account shadowing. Kept minimum handoff/acceptance for all, prioritized 12 readiness sessions, and defined the transition fallback.
Customer continuity
Naledi Kavanagh / current facts

Recommendation and decision statement
Recommendation: execute the P11 transfer exactly as listed, with the mandatory acceptance, customer-contact, and continuity controls above; do not defer it for exhaustive shadowing. Decision: Ivy Marchbanks will proceed with the 31-account commercial-landscape transition on the assigned 04, 11, and 18 Nov 2026 waves, accepting the current-term −$47,754 FY26-through-P10 commission impact as the known cost of concentrating the new segment in the inside-sales desk.

spec.professional_context: Wholesale irrigation-supply sales operations at a regional business-unit level, where a field-account transition must be communicated accurately and credibly to an experienced sales representative and senior leadership.
difficulty_sources: Reconcile a complete account-level transition from one review packet while preserving changed facts over a prior draft.
Derive and repeat a defensible commission impact without inventing compensation protection.
Resolve a genuine time/capacity tradeoff and draw an unobvious must/should boundary.
Communicate one difficult decision candidly to both the affected veteran representative and senior leadership within a short operating-plan format.

reference_file.construction: Create one offline workbook serving as the sole source packet. Include a current account roster with synthetic account IDs/names, segment classification, current owner, transfer designation, effective P11 timing or wave, revenue/commission-relevant figures, and continuity flags. Include commission terms sufficient to recompute Dale's baseline, the transferred-book amount, and the resulting impact. Include a working draft reflecting earlier assumptions, plus explicit review comments from the named reviewers and a changed-facts section that supersedes the draft where applicable. Ensure all sheets are mutually consistent and that exactly 31 distinct accounts are designated for transfer. Include at least some retained accounts for comparison and meaningful continuity-sensitive cases among the transferred accounts. Use Quimby account names plus Longbarrow Manufacturing and Marlowe Associates as plausible organisations in the packet. Make the review comments create a real revision task, especially around ordering the loss/gain framing, account completeness, timing, commission clarity, customer continuity, and the must/should boundary. Do not include hidden answer text or rubric language.

rules: The gold plan lists exactly the 31 distinct source-designated transfer accounts, each once, and preserves source timing/status distinctions.
All commission figures are derived from the supplied commission terms and transferred-account figures; repeated figures reconcile within one dollar.
Material changed facts supersede the working draft, and the change record maps those revisions to packet comments or changed facts.
The plan makes one recommendation, explicitly prioritizes must-do pre-effective-date controls under limited time and desk capacity, and identifies a workable fallback during transition.
The plan assigns owners, customer handoff controls, escalation triggers, and a monitoring check using source-supported or ordinary professional operating practice.
The document is candid and respectful to Dale, places gains and losses in a comparable frame, remains within three pages, and ends with the decision.
gold_derivation.intended_verdict: A strong reference solution is a concise, decision-ready DOCX with a highly legible account table or equivalent complete account view, reconciled commission math, explicit revision traceability, practical continuity controls, and one defensible recommendation. It must not invent compensation protection or operational facts.

tensions: Limited time and inside-sales onboarding capacity make exhaustive pre-transition shadowing impossible, requiring a defensible staged fallback.
The document must distinguish commitments that are mandatory for continuity and fairness from desirable improvements that cannot be guaranteed immediately.
difficulty_alignment.transformation_chain: Read the review packet and changed facts; reconcile the current transfer population and timing; derive the commission effect; convert the result into an audience-specific operating plan with owners, controls, and one decision.

reference_files.purpose: Source packet containing the current account roster and segment classifications, commission terms and figures, the working transition draft, explicit review comments, and changed operational facts needed to revise the plan.
reference_files.discovery: Open the workbook in the working directory; use it as the sole source for account-level facts, commission calculations, timing, and review changes.

deliverables.description: A decision-ready territory transition operating plan for Dale Prendergast and senior leadership.
constraints: Top level of the starting working directory; exactly three pages or fewer; must include the complete transfer view, commission effect, transition ownership and customer handoff expectations, response to review comments and changed facts, and one final recommendation/decision statement. No system click-through instructions or compensation-policy rewrite.
